name: cwd-literal-plus
description: A literal '+' in cwd survives decoding as a '+'. This is the case that separates RFC 3986 path-segment unescaping from query unescaping: the latter would silently turn '+' into a space.
grounding: Readers percent-decode with RFC 3986 path-segment rules (PathUnescape), not query rules (QueryUnescape). '+' is not in the producer's encode set, so it crosses the wire verbatim and must decode back to itself.
notes: Roundtrip because '+' is outside the percent-encode set (C0, DEL, space, '%', '"', '\\', and every byte >= 0x80), so the producer emits it raw. Without this case a reader could switch to query unescaping and the whole corpus would stay green while every path or session name containing a '+' silently lost it to a space.
